result.title: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: Dynamics-Aware Benchmarking of Protein Motif Scaffolding
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track). 23 pages, 10 figures, including supplementary material. The first three authors contributed equally. BILBY-PRO dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/HFMI-PROFOUND/BILBY-PRO ; BILBY-MD code: https://github.com/PROFOUND-HFMI/BILBY-MD
result.summary: Protein motif scaffolding benchmarks assess whether generative models can build scaffolds around functionally important residues. Their conclusions depend on which motifs are tested and which criteria define success. Existing benchmarks typically use small hand-curated motif sets and static refolding criteria, but protein function often depends on conformational ensembles and transitions. Here, we address both benchmark scope and success criteria. We introduce BILBY-PRO, a systematically derived benchmark of structurally conserved functional motifs from PROSITE-linked experimental structures, comprising 220 cases from 174 PROSITE motif-pattern entries. Evaluating six recent scaffold-generation models reveals distinct patterns in target coverage and unique-solution yield: RFDiffusion and Proteina solve more targets, whereas ESM3 produces more unique successful scaffolds on the targets it solves. We further introduce BILBY-MD, a reference-based all-atom molecular dynamics evaluation framework. Applied to statically solved designs from the original MotifBench benchmark, it compares motif drift, scaffold drift, motif-contact preservation, and motif-dihedral free-energy landscapes against reference simulations. Of 55 statically solved model-problem pairs, 31 satisfy our MD-supported criterion and only 8 pass all checks. Compact, self-contained motifs are often MD-supported, whereas interface-like or context-dependent motifs fail more frequently. Static refolding success therefore provides useful evidence of local motif recovery but does not establish dynamical fidelity of the full scaffold. BILBY highlights three complementary axes of motif-scaffolding evaluation: target coverage, unique-solution yield, and MD-supported dynamical fidelity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 BILBY-PRO 蛋白 motif scaffolding 基准（220 例，源自 PROSITE 关联结构）并比较六个生成模型，同时提出基于参考全原子分子动力学的 BILBY-MD 评估框架，发现多数静态 refolding 成功的解并不能通过动态保真检查。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「静态通过率不等于动力学保真」的评价思路可能为 LVR 评价提供线索：是否仅检验最终答案、还是需检验推理轨迹与潜在状态的动态保真及证据保持，可供核查；但研究对象是蛋白设计，与视觉推理无直接联系。
